Triggers.value: The same time of day the event occurred

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).
Dates or anniversaries connected to the event
I spend money impulsively to distract or comfort myself

Memory.value: There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy

vignette: Maria, a 66-year-old shopowner of Oceania ethnicity, has been struggling with persistent distress since an incident of police violence at her small store nearly three years ago. The traumatic event occurred late in the evening, around 8 PM, and involved a series of aggressive confrontations that left Maria feeling both physically shaken and deeply violated. Since then, certain triggers have taken on potent meanings for her. At the same time each day—around 8 PM—Maria begins to experience intense feelings of being watched or observed, accompanied by bouts of dizziness and lightheadedness. These sensations are so powerful that she avoids any activity at this hour, even closing her store earlier than usual to preempt these overwhelming experiences. The feeling of being watched is exacerbated when she finds herself in dark environments reminiscent of the event, leading Maria to adopt strict avoidance strategies. Maria’s memory of the event is fragmented and disjointed. She often cannot recall specific details or moments from that night; instead, they are replaced by vague and unsettling sensations. This makes it difficult for her to put the events into words, further complicating how she processes what happened. The memory feels so surreal that Maria questions its veracity, even though the physical scars remain. Maria has developed a strong sense of inadequacy since the event, believing that her reactions show she is an inadequate and lousy coper. She fears that her responses to triggers mean she might be going crazy. These negative appraisals have a significant impact on her memory; the more she feels like she’s losing control or becoming crazy, the less coherent her memories of the trauma become. To cope with these overwhelming feelings, Maria has turned to compulsive spending as a way to distract herself and gain some semblance of control over her life. However, this behavior often leads to financial strain and exacerbates her feeling of inadequacy. The more she spends impulsively, the worse she feels about her ability to manage and cope with stress. The memory gaps and nonverbal nature of her trauma have led Maria to avoid anniversaries and specific dates related to the event. She finds herself struggling with intrusive thoughts and flashbacks during these times, which further reinforce her negative appraisals and lead to more episodes of feeling dizzy or lightheaded. Each time she feels watched or experiences dizziness, it triggers a cycle that spirals into deeper self-doubt and avoidance. Maria’s daily life has become significantly impacted by these dynamics. She often closes the shop early on days when she anticipates an anniversary or any other trigger might occur. This has affected her business operations and strained relationships with long-time customers who rely on the store being open during those hours. The compounded effects of this cycle have been overwhelming for Maria. Her sense of self-worth is increasingly eroded by these recurrent experiences, leaving her feeling more isolated and uncertain about how to navigate her daily life without constantly triggering further distress. Finally, she has decided to seek help, hoping that a therapist can provide strategies to break the cycle and regain some semblance of normalcy in her life. What frightens Maria most is the prospect of continuing on this path indefinitely, unable to control or understand why these memories and feelings persist. She is hopeful that with support and guidance, she might be able to reclaim her sense of self and begin healing from the trauma.
